jobs.description:
This position is responsible for managing Modivcare's external communications function, with functional ownership of media relations, press materials, social media, and evergreen PR content for the corporate brand. Reporting to the Director, Corporate Communications, this role serves as the primary point of contact for media inquiries, proactively builds and maintains relationships with healthcare and business journalists, and executes the full lifecycle of earned media activity — from proactive pitching and press release drafting to reactive response and coverage tracking. This role partners cross-functionally to ensure consistency between external messaging and employee-facing communications and collaborates with marketing communications and government and public affairs on relevant external channel content.

This role...

Manages Modivcare's media relations program, serving as the primary corporate contact for inbound media inquiries and proactively pitching stories, commentary, and executive perspectives to healthcare, business, and trade press.
Develops and maintains relationships with journalists, editors, and reporters covering healthcare services and Medicaid managed care, building a durable network that supports earned media objectives.
Drafts, edits, and distributes press releases, media statements, op-eds, and letters to the editor, ensuring accuracy, message alignment, and adherence to brand voice and legal review requirements.
Owns the corporate library of evergreen PR content — including executive biographies, corporate fact sheets, boilerplate language, and approved talking points — maintaining currency and consistency across all external materials.
Creates corporate social media strategy, developing and executing a content calendar that reflects the company's external communications priorities, brand standards, and audience engagement goals, with support from external agency partners as applicable.
Develops strategy and supporting materials for tradeshows.
Monitors corporate social media channels and the broader media landscape for coverage, sentiment, and emerging narratives relevant to Modivcare, escalating issues through appropriate channels.
Coordinates the development of speaking opportunity materials — including speaker abstracts, presentation support content, and award submissions.
Partners with internal communications to ensure alignment between external messaging and employee-facing communications, particularly during significant announcements, organizational changes, or reputational events.
Collaborates with marketing communications on external channel content that intersects with the corporate website, ensuring that PR-driven content and brand-driven content are consistent and mutually reinforcing.
Collaborates with government and public affairs on external channel content that intersects with key policy priorities and milestones.
Measures and reports on earned media performance, social media engagement, and external channel effectiveness.
Supports crisis and incident response communications by preparing draft external statements, monitoring media activity, and coordinating timely distribution of approved materials.
May lead projects and perform other duties as assigned; occasional business travel may be required.

We are interested in speaking to individuals with the following...

Bachelor's Degree in Communications, Public Relations, Journalism, or a related field required.
Seven (7) plus years of experience in media relations, public relations, or external communications required.
Experience in a healthcare, healthcare services, or Medicaid managed care environment preferred.
Or equivalent combination of education and/or experience.
Proven experience in media relations, public relations, or external communications, with a demonstrated track record of securing earned media coverage and managing journalist relationships in a corporate or agency environment.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to draft clear, accurate, and compelling press materials, statements, and social content across a range of formats and audiences.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple concurrent workstreams — including proactive media outreach, reactive inquiry response, and content production — with strong attention to detail and consistent follow-through.
Strong understanding of the earned media landscape, including how healthcare and business press operates, what drives coverage, and how to position corporate narratives effectively with relevant media outlets.
Familiarity with social media management practices for corporate channels, including content planning, publishing, community monitoring, and performance measurement.
Proven ability to build and maintain productive working relationships with external stakeholders, including journalists, agency partners, and industry contacts.
Strong project management skills, with the ability to prioritize competing demands and meet deadlines in a fast-paced, regulated environment.
Demonstrated ability to exercise sound judgment and discretion when handling sensitive information, including pre-announcement materials, crisis-related content, and executive communications.
Working knowledge of the healthcare services industry, including the regulatory and reputational dynamics of Medicaid-funded programs; experience in healthcare or Medicaid managed care preferred.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and familiarity with content management systems, social media management platforms, and media monitoring tools.
Ability to navigate a complex, matrixed organization and collaborate effectively across functions, including legal, investor relations, human resources, and business unit communications teams.

Summary

Job Summary

The Division of Natural Sciences encourages applications for the Senior Communications Specialist position! This role supports the Division of Natural Sciences (NSCI) in the College of Arts and Sciences to develop, plan, lead, and coordinate strategic communications that highlight research, academic programs, student opportunities, and achievements for an external audience. As a member of the college communications team, this position serves as a critical connector between NSCI, college, and university communications partners to support the reputation, recruitment, and retention priorities of NSCI, especially as they relate to college strategic priorities and campus institutional priorities. This position reports to the assistant dean for communications.

The individual in this role must have a strong communications background and excellent skills in organization and prioritization. To facilitate the required activities, the individual must be knowledgeable of the division and its 14 departments and Public Health program as well as college and campus communication strategies and standard processes. Further, the successful candidate must have a demonstrated ability to independently handle multiple self-directed projects that may, at times, have contending priorities and due dates.

CU is an Equal Opportunity Employer and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment. We are committed to creating a workplace where all individuals are treated with respect and dignity, and we encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply, including protected veterans and individuals with disabilities.

Who We Are

The College of Arts and Sciences at the University of Colorado Boulder is the intellectual core of the university, conducting research, scholarship, creative work and education in more than 60 fields. Our research generates new knowledge, solving some of the world’s most critical problems!

The college leads nationally in undergraduate and graduate education in the natural sciences, social sciences and arts and humanities, bringing world-class research and scholarship to our students, both in and out of the classroom.

Responsibilities

What Your Key Responsibilities Will Be

Coordinate and Advance NSCI Communications

Serve as the primary communications liaison for departments and programs to coordinate and advance NSCI communication priorities. Maintain partnerships with communicators in related institutes to coordinate stories and announcements, and to broaden reach.
Serve as the communications expert advising department leadership, faculty and staff on communicating department strengths through compelling storytelling.
Collaborate with department leadership and the college’s director of editorial communications to find opportunities to increase NSCI visibility, media engagement and strategic promotion opportunities.
Advise division and department leadership on defining objectives, messaging, audiences and metrics for diverse communications needs across the division.
Advise departments on connecting communications with broader college priorities, campus institutional priorities and current events for greater amplification.
Collaborate with college communications colleagues to advise departments on integrated marketing and communications strategies, content planning and standard processes across web, social media and other digital communications channels to advance NSCI.
Facilitate external communications including requests for interviews, news releases and media requests for experts in partnership with college and campus communications. Partner with the university’s Strategic Relations and Communications team to prepare faculty and staff for positive engagement with the media.
Identify trends, opportunities and audience insights to inform communications planning and priorities.

Develop, Produce and Lead NSCI Communications

Independently design, develop and implement strategic communications plans in collaboration with department, division and college communications leadership that address a complex array of situations, scopes and assignments.
Produce news articles, web copy, social posts, multimedia and other content for publication across NSCI, college and campus channels.
Provide project development and management to build out the division’s critical communications infrastructure and strengthen the division’s visual identity.
Design products and processes that support departmental communications needs at scale.
Work with internal and external partners to ensure messages reach the intended audiences (media, university leadership, partners and the public).
Develop NSCI communications for distribution through the university email marketing platform.
Identify, lead and contribute to college communications campaigns that originate in NSCI, such as new degrees, program name changes or new program launches.
Create and curate compelling visuals for social media and websites within the college’s Digital Asset Management system.

Other

Regularly analyze and deliver market and audience insights and tracking to NSCI leadership on reach, digital engagement, and communications effectiveness.
Support college communications initiatives and projects as assigned.
Participate in professional development activities.
May supervise student employees supporting communications and content development activities.

What You Should Know

The work schedule for this hybrid position is Monday-Friday, 8-5 p.m., with a minimum of 3 in-person days per week. May require more in-person days as needed.

What We Can Offer

The annual salary for this full-time position is $70,900 - $75,000. Onboarding assistance may be available.

Benefits

At the University of Colorado Boulder , we are committed to supporting the holistic health and well-being of our employees. Our comprehensive benefits package includes medical, dental, and retirement plans; generous paid time off; tuition assistance for you and your dependents; and an ECO Pass for local transit. As one of Boulder County’s largest employers, CU Boulder offers an inspiring academic community and access to world-class outdoor recreation. Explore additional perks and programs through the CU Advantage program.

Be Statements

Be creative. Be impactful. Be Boulder.

What We Require

Bachelor’s degree in journalism, communication, public relations, marketing or another relevant field.
3+ years of professional-level experience in journalism, communications, public relations, marketing or related field.
A combination of relevant education, training and/or experience may substitute on a year-for-year basis.

What You Will Need

Demonstrated commitment to promoting diverse and inclusive communications and communities.
Sensitivity to and appreciation of cultural, political and geographical differences with the ability to work effectively with faculty, staff and students from around the world.
Strong organizational, prioritization and time-management skills.
Ability to handle multiple tasks, priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced and collaborative environment.
Ability to adapt to changing situations and priorities.
Ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a complex organizational environment.

What We Would Like You To Have

5+ years of professional-level experience in journalism, communications, public relations, or marketing.
Experience working in a higher education environment.
Experience writing and developing content related to research, science, or other technical subject matter.
Demonstrated experience developing integrated strategic communications content across multiple platforms and audiences.
Familiarity with email marketing and content management systems.
Familiarity with social media platforms.
Experience using Adobe Creative Suite and/or basic photography and multimedia tools.
Demonstrated ability to build collaborative relationships and support a customer-focused communications environment

The Alberta Public Service
works to build a stronger province for current and future generations. We make a difference in the lives of Albertans through rewarding and diverse career opportunities.

The Alberta Human Rights Commission works with Albertans to promote awareness of, and appreciation for, human rights and diversity. Its overall goal is to develop inclusive communities in which all Albertans can participate in the social, economic, and cultural life of the province without discrimination.

Created by the Government of Alberta, the Commission is an independent commission that reports to the Minister of Justice. It has a two-fold mandate: to foster equality and to reduce discrimination. It fulfills this mandate through the resolution and settlement of human rights complaints; an administratively fair human rights tribunal process, and through education programs, policy development, and collaborative initiatives.

Role Responsibilities

Are you ready to shape public understanding of human rights in Alberta? This role offers a unique opportunity to develop and implement communications that promote human rights, inform Albertans, and highlight the vital programs and services of the Alberta Human Rights Commission.

Reporting to the Director, Communication, Education and Engagement (CEE), you will lead and support diverse marketing and communications initiatives. This challenging yet rewarding position requires strategic thinking, creativity, and the ability to translate complex human rights issues into clear, accessible messages for a wide range of audiences.

As Communications Consultant, you will lead content creation, develop comprehensive communication plans, and support both internal and external communications initiatives. You'll collaborate closely with internal subject matter experts and CEE colleagues to ensure effective and timely delivery of key messages across various platforms.

Your responsibilities in this role will include but will not be limited to

Developing and executing comprehensive marketing and communications strategies for internal and external audiences, including media relations, digital content, and brand management.
Leading the development and planning for new communication vehicles like newsletters and other digital communication mediums.
Creating and editing engaging, plain language content for diverse platforms like websites, social media, newsletters, reports, and speeches, ensuring accessibility and clarity.
Leading public awareness campaigns and initiatives that increase awareness and understanding of human rights and the Commission.
Conducting research and environmental scans to identify trends and inform strategic communication decisions.
Providing expert communications advice and support, including issues management, strategic planning, and plain language audits and reviews.

To be successful in this role you will need to demonstrate:

Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with a proven ability to craft clear, concise, and engaging plain language content.
Strategic thinking for developing and implementing effective marketing and communication plans.
Strong project management abilities to lead initiatives from concept to evaluation.
Excellent interpersonal and collaboration skills for engaging diverse internal and external stakeholders.
Proficiency with digital communication tools (e.g., Adobe, Canva, email marketing platforms, social media management tools) and content management systems.
Strong knowledge and understanding of social justice principles, such as equity, root causes, diversity, inclusion, racism, and discrimination.

The Job Description is provided for Further details on this position.

APS Competencies

Competencies are behaviors that are essential to reach our goals in serving Albertans. We encourage you to have an in depth understanding of the competencies that are required for this opportunity and to be prepared to demonstrate them during the recruitment process.

Below Are The Critical Competencies Required For This Role

Agility - Must be able to anticipate, assess, and readily adapt to changing priorities, maintain resilience, and work effectively in changing environments.
Develop Networks - Proactively builds networks, foster connections, and establishes trust in relationships with diverse stakeholders.

jobs.title: Head of Communications
jobs.description:
About Us

OneMain Financial (NYSE: OMF) is the leader in offering nonprime consumers responsible access to credit and is dedicated to improving the financial well-being of hardworking Americans. With more than 1,300 retail locations supported by digital capabilities and centralized operations, we serve nearly 4 million customers in 48 states through personal loans, auto finance, credit cards, and insurance products designed to help people meet their financial needs today and progress to a stronger future. Since 1912, we have combined the scale, stability, and resources of a national financial services company with the personal relationships, care, and local market knowledge of community-based teams. Today, our more than 9,300 team members are building on that legacy by applying data science, technology, and new ideas to enhance the customer experience, strengthen our business, and support long-term growth.

At OneMain, team members take on challenging, purposeful work in a collaborative and ethical environment where people are respected, contributions are recognized, and leaders are committed to development. Whether serving customers directly or enabling the people, capabilities, and operations that power our business, our team members have opportunities to expand their skills, advance their careers, and make a meaningful impact in the communities where we live and work.

The Role

OneMain Financial is seeking an experienced executive for VP/MD
Head of Corporate Communications
.

This critical leadership role will develop and lead the company’s overarching communications strategy in support of OneMain’s business objectives, reputation, culture, and relationships with key stakeholders. Reporting to the Head of External Affairs, the Head of Corporate Communications will serve as a trusted advisor to the CEO and senior leadership team on executive communications, employee communications, media relations, reputation management, and significant business and policy developments. This leader will translate OneMain’s strategic priorities into an integrated communications roadmap and establish the operating cadence, capabilities, and measurement framework needed to execute it effectively.

The successful candidate will be a strong enterprise collaborator, partnering closely with External Affairs, Finance, Investor Relations, Human Resources, Legal, Compliance, Operations, Marketing, and Technology. This is an opportunity to build and develop a best-in-class Corporate Communications function as OneMain continues to grow and evolve.

Key Responsibilities

Develop and own OneMain’s enterprise communications strategy, aligning communications priorities and resources with the company’s business objectives.
Serve as a trusted advisor to the CEO and senior leadership team on communications strategy, executive positioning, sensitive announcements, stakeholder messaging, and reputation management.
Develop and oversee the company’s internal communications strategy and operating cadence, including enterprise announcements, leadership communications, companywide meetings, cultural narratives, and annual and quarterly business updates.
Establish clear communications standards, processes, and governance to promote consistency, accuracy, appropriate review, and alignment across internal and external communications.
Develop and execute communications strategies that support effective change management, ensuring that companywide changes, new policies, and strategic shifts are communicated clearly, consistently, and through appropriate channels and cadences.
Partner closely with the Head of External Affairs to develop and execute strategies relating to media relations, executive thought leadership, issues management, public affairs, and proactive corporate storytelling.
Protect and enhance OneMain’s reputation among employees, customers, investors, regulators, policymakers, the media, community partners, and other key stakeholders.
Lead executive communications, including speeches, presentations, leadership messages, employee communications, external statements, talking points, and other materials for the CEO and senior executives.
Lead communications supporting significant business events and developments, including, regulatory matters, acquisitions, policy developments, organizational changes, and strategic initiatives. Support communications related to quarterly earnings.
Lead media relations in partnership with External Affairs, including proactive engagement, response strategy, message development, media preparation, and relationship-building with relevant national, financial-services, trade, and local media.
Oversee issues and crisis communications, including preparedness, escalation protocols, scenario planning, executive counsel, rapid-response messaging, and coordination with Legal, Compliance, Risk, and other relevant functions.
Monitor and analyze media coverage, stakeholder sentiment, industry developments, policy trends, and emerging reputational issues, and provide timely insights and recommendations to senior leadership and other internal audiences.
Develop a communications measurement framework that uses meaningful data and insights to assess effectiveness, inform strategy, and demonstrate impact against business and reputational objectives.
Manage external communications agencies and vendors, including scopes of work, resource allocation, performance expectations, budgets, and periodic reviews.
Build, lead, and develop a high-performing Corporate Communications team, including defining roles and responsibilities, strengthening capabilities, and planning for succession in critical positions.
Manage the Corporate Communications budget and headcount plan, ensuring that resources remain aligned with changing business needs and priorities.
Evaluate and responsibly deploy communications technologies, including generative artificial intelligence tools, in alignment with OneMain’s legal, compliance, cybersecurity, privacy, and technology-governance standards.
Travel: up to 30% domestic travel

Required Qualifications

Approximately 10 years of experience in corporate communications, executive communications, public affairs, media relations, or a related field, with increasing levels of responsibility.
Bachelor's degree in Communications, Journalism, Public Relations, Business, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
Experience leading communications teams or significant communications initiatives in a corporate, public company, highly regulated, or public affairs environment.
Experience developing and executing communications strategies that support business priorities.
Experience advising senior executives on communications related to business, organizational, or reputational matters.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex business, financial, regulatory, or policy topics into clear, compelling communications for a variety of audiences.
Experience developing executive, employee, and stakeholder communications across multiple channels.
Sound judgment and experience supporting issues management, organizational change, crisis communications, or other high-profile business situations.
Demonstrated ability to build strong relationships, influence across functions, and work effectively in a fast-paced environment.
Experience using data, insights, or feedback to measure communications effectiveness and inform strategy.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in financial services, banking, consumer finance, insurance, healthcare, or another regulated industry.
Experience partnering with Legal, Compliance, Investor Relations, Human Resources, Government Relations, or Public Policy teams.
Experience leading or helping evolve a corporate communications function, team, or communications strategy.
Experience in both in-house corporate communications and agency environments.
Familiarity with generative AI tools and emerging communications technologies.

Target base salary range is $250,000 - $275,000
which is based on various factors including skills and work experience. In addition to base salary, this role is eligible for a competitive bonus compensation program that is based on individual and company performance.

Because team members at their best means OneMain at our best, we provide opportunities and benefits that make their health and careers a priority. That is why we have packed our comprehensive benefits package with:

Health and well-being options for team members and their dependents
Up to 4% matching 401(k)

Bonus eligible

jobs.description:
Job Profile Summary

Broward College, located in sunny South Florida, is one of the largest state colleges in the country. With an enrollment of approximately 50,000 students supported by 4,000 employees, the College was rated as a best-in-state employer by Forbes and a top community college by the Aspen Institute.

Under the leadership of its President and Chief Executive Officer, Broward College is building on a strong foundation while advancing a bold vision for the future. We seek an experienced and innovative strategic leader in marketing and communications to help elevate the College’s reputation and position Broward College as the number one destination for academic excellence!

Broward College is searching nationally for a new Vice President of Strategic Communication and Marketing. We seek an extraordinary leader to join an exceptional institution. The individual selected for this leadership role will thrive in a culture that pursues excellence while maintaining the highest level of respect for each other as colleagues, someone who embraces our responsibility to serve each other, our students, and our community.

The Vice President of Strategic Communication and Marketing reports to the College President and will play a critical role in defining, developing, and implementing effective marketing and public relations strategies to enhance the institution's brand and boost student recruitment, enrollment, and retention. This role will involve a deep understanding of the student journey, from initial attraction to successful completion and placement. The ideal individual has deep expertise in the marketing funnel up to and including conversion, with a proven track record in building, cultivating, and refining brands to increase visibility and strengthen the institution’s reputation.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Planning & Implementation

Work closely with the President to shape and execute a comprehensive, action-oriented marketing and public relations strategy that aligns with the College's mission.

Craft and cast a compelling value proposition to prospective students, highlighting the strengths, uniqueness, and opportunities Broward College offers.

Analyze and map the entire student life cycle, focusing on conversion rates at every stage of the student experience.

Routinely Examine The Market To Address Key Questions, Including

What's the current and future state of the market landscape?
Who makes up our student population in terms of demographics and psychographics?
Which programs attract the most enrollments, and what drives their popularity?

Designs, manages, and reports outcome measurements for each initiative. Provides strategic plans to meet initiatives. Reviews site analytics and recommends strategies for search engine optimization, internet advertising, and the effective development and integration of social media with traditional marketing.

Provides strategic direction and leadership for college-wide marketing and communications, including, but not limited to, branding, creative services, outreach services and integrated campaigns, institutional advertising, social media, public/media relations, communications, community engagement, and outreach activities.

Understands and embraces the role of traditional media in a comprehensive, strategic communications action plan to achieve organizational goals.

Work closely with Student Services to understand and develop strategies to bolster student retention and completion rates.

Understands crisis communications management using NIMS/ICS protocols, including updates for the media and internal and external audiences using established communication channels (i.e., Hotlines, College website, emergency notification system.)

Team Leadership & Development

Lead, coach, and develop a marketing and public relations professional team, ensuring they align with the College's strategic objectives.

Collaborate with other departments, faculty, and external stakeholders to ensure a unified marketing and public relations approach.

Qualifications

Master’s degree in marketing, communications, or related field.
A minimum of 10 years of experience in marketing, communications, or a similar field, including five years in management.
A strategic thinker with the ability to develop a long-term strategic marketing plan as well as the ability to acknowledge and seize imminent opportunities.
A leader who knows how to execute and operationalize a vision.
A detail-oriented, creative, proactive, dynamic, and positive professional.
Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to inspire and mobilize diverse teams and stakeholders.
Strong ethical standards and a commitment to Broward College’s values and mission.
An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.

Our Culture

At Broward College, our leaders embody a culture of competence, care, character, composure, and courage. We prioritize serving each other and our students through high-quality guidance, mutual respect, resilience, and fair, thoughtful decision-making, all while upholding the values of integrity, transparency, and honesty.

Broward College offers an exceptional benefits package including, but not limited to:

Healthcare Insurance (Medical, Dental & Vision)
Retirement Options – Florida Retirement System (FRS) Pension Plan or the FRS Investment Plan
Wellness Program
Vacation/Paid Time Off
Winter and Spring Break College Closures
Paid Parental Leave
Tuition Reimbursement and Tuition Assistance (available to employees and family members)

About Broward College

Broward College is a nationally ranked institution of higher education in Broward County, Florida, providing residents and non-residents with access to high-quality, affordable education.

The College offers several areas of study, including certificate programs, two-year university-transfer degrees, two-year career degrees, bachelor's degrees, and continuing education courses.

Broward College is the largest institution of higher education in Broward County, serving approximately 50,000 students annually. Around half of our students are Pell grant recipients, and approximately half of our students are first generation college students. With more than 4,000 colleagues,

Broward College serves as a critical economic engine for Broward College, generating more than 1.7 billion in economic impact for Broward County, and driving opportunities for economic mobility for all of Broward County.

Broward College has been repeatedly recognized as one of the top 10 community colleges in America by the Aspen Institute. The College continues to receive recognition for its transformational work to improve institutional culture and care for its employees as recognized by the College and University Professional Association for Human Resources (CUPA-HR) 2022 National HR Excellence Award.

As an equal access and employment opportunity institution, Broward College is committed to a tradition of increasing and retaining an intellectually, culturally, and ethnically diverse student body and workforce and focusing on the success of our students, faculty, and staff while strengthening our local and global communities.

Freeborn Mower Electric Cooperative (FMEC) invites applications for the position of VP Marketing & External Relations in Albert Lea, MN and has selected Dairyland Power Cooperative to facilitate the search process.

Freeborn Mower Electric Cooperative is a member-owned electric cooperative serving primarily Freeborn and Mower Counties in southern Minnesota. Founded in 1936, FMEC has been part of the community for more than 85 years and today serves more than 18,000 member-owners across a 1,235-square-mile service territory. The cooperative is committed to delivering safe and reliable power, dependable energy solutions, helpful programs and a positive experience for every member. Governed by a nine-member board elected by the membership and supported by a skilled local workforce, FMEC is a not-for-profit cooperative grounded in the Seven Cooperative Principles. Local ownership, community accountability and long-term member trust guide FMEC’s work as it supports economic growth, local initiatives and the well-being of the communities it serves. The Vice President of Marketing and External Relations will play a key leadership role in strengthening FMEC’s member communications, public presence, community partnerships and engagement with local stakeholders.

The Vice President of Marketing & External Relations reports to the President & CEO and leads the Communications and Marketing Team, Energy Solutions Team and Member Services Team. jobs.description:
University Overview

The University of Pennsylvania, the largest private employer in Philadelphia, is a world-renowned leader in education, research, and innovation. This historic, Ivy League school consistently ranks among the top 10 universities in the annual U.S. News & World Report survey. Penn has 12 highly-regarded schools that provide opportunities for undergraduate, graduate and continuing education, all influenced by Penn’s distinctive interdisciplinary approach to scholarship and learning. As an employer Penn has been ranked nationally on many occasions with the most recent award from Forbes who named Penn one of America’s Best Large Employers in 2023.

Penn offers a unique working environment within the city of Philadelphia. The University is situated on a beautiful urban campus, with easy access to a range of educational, cultural, and recreational activities. With its historical significance and landmarks, lively cultural offerings, and wide variety of atmospheres, Philadelphia is the perfect place to call home for work and play.

The University offers a competitive benefits package that includes excellent healthcare and tuition benefits for employees and their families, generous retirement benefits, a wide variety of professional development opportunities, supportive work and family benefits, a wealth of health and wellness programs and resources, and much more.

Posted Job Title

Digital Communications & Web Manager

Job Profile Title

Manager, Marketing

Job Description Summary

The Digital Communications & Web Manager is responsible for managing and enhancing the organization's digital presence through website administration, social media engagement, and strategic digital communications. This role oversees website content within the LiveWhale content management system, develops compelling social media and marketing campaigns, and creates engaging digital content that supports institutional priorities, events, and initiatives. The ideal candidate is a creative and detail-oriented communicator with strong writing, technical, and project management skills who thrives in a collaborative, fast-paced environment and is passionate about digital storytelling, audience engagement, and maintaining a consistent and impactful brand presence to help drive enrollment and philanthropy.

Reporting to the Executive Director of Marketing, Communications and Events, the Digital Communications and Web Manager is responsible for the development, deployment, and management of marketing campaigns and web pages for Penn Nursing’s academic programs. The Manager will work with numerous colleagues and units and must be excellent at cross-functional collaboration, project management, and verbal and written communication. Responsibilities include deployment and oversight of advertising campaigns across multiple platforms and channels, email campaigns through Slate CRM, with the Admissions Department, and an email marketing platform, campaign performance reporting, email and landing page templates, and A/B testing. The person in this role will be responsible for working with a creative team on the development of engaging and effective ads, collateral, and communications. Website responsibilities will include oversight of academic program web pages, optimizing web pages for conversion, use of Google Tag Manager, data analysis through Google Analytics and Google Data Studio, Meta and LinkedIn, and A/B testing for continual improvement. The Manager will liaise with colleagues in the Office of Admissions for enrollment marketing campaign planning and also the development team to determine audience and key messaging development, as well as program feasibility. 

Reponsibilities/Duties

Job Description

Digital Marketing

Develop and implement digital marketing strategies that support institutional priorities, events, academic programs, and recruitment initiatives.
Manage and execute multiple digital marketing and advertising campaigns with varying timelines, including audience development, website updates, creative asset coordination, campaign implementation, and performance analysis.
Support email marketing campaigns, promotional outreach, and audience communications.
Coordinate with the branding and creative team to develop digital assets, including graphics, photography, video, and web content.
Monitor campaign performance and engagement metrics, providing regular progress updates, final reports, and recommendations for continuous improvement.
Collaborate closely with communications, marketing, and leadership teams to ensure consistent messaging, brand alignment, and successful execution of strategic initiatives.

Project Management

Lead digital and marketing projects from conception through completion, including planning, execution, monitoring, reporting, and post-project evaluation.
Utilize project management tools and best practices to coordinate workflows, prioritize tasks, and ensure projects are delivered on time, within scope, and within budget.
Manage project timelines, quality standards, and resources while balancing competing priorities across multiple initiatives.
Facilitate project debriefs and after-action reviews to identify successes, lessons learned, and opportunities to improve future campaigns and processes.
Coordinate cross-functional teams, vendors, and stakeholders to ensure project milestones, deliverables, and communication remain aligned throughout the project lifecycle.

Website Management

Manage and update website content using White Whale / LiveWhale CMS
Build and maintain webpages, news stories, profiles, event listings, and multimedia content
Ensure website content is accurate, accessible, user-friendly, and aligned with brand standards
Monitor website performance and recommend improvements for usability and engagement
Coordinate with internal stakeholders on web updates and digital projects

Social Media & Digital Communications

Develop, schedule, and publish social media content across platforms including LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X/Twitter, and YouTube
Create engaging digital campaigns that support organizational priorities, events, programs, and initiatives
Assist with content planning, copywriting, and visual storytelling
Monitor analytics and engagement metrics to inform strategy and improve performance
Support livestreams, video promotion, and digital event coverage as needed

Job Location - City, State

Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree with at least three years in communications, marketing, journalism, digital media, or related field
Experience managing websites using White Whale / LiveWhale or similar CMS platforms
Creative thinker and team player, possessing integrity, discretion, and excellent judgment. Brings a positive attitude and willingness to help other team members.
Strong understanding of social media strategy and digital marketing best practices
Excellent writing, editing, and organizational skills
Experience using Canva, Adobe Creative Suite, or similar design tools
High skill level and experience with SEO/SEM, website funnel design, Slate or other CRM, Google Tag Manager, Google Analytics, Meta, LinkedIn, and Data Studio
Familiarity with analytics tools, SEO principles, and email marketing platforms preferred
Ability to manage multiple deadlines and work collaboratively across teams

Preferred Skills

Experience in higher education, healthcare, nonprofit, or mission-driven organizations
Photography/video editing experience a plus
Strong attention to detail and ability to work independently
Superior interpersonal skills with the ability to build and maintain effective professional relationships.
Knowledge of accessibility and web content standards

Department / School

School of Nursing

Pay Range

$65,628.00 - $82,000.00 Annual Rate

Salary offers are made based on the candidate’s qualifications, experience, skills, and education as they directly relate to the requirements of the position, and in alignment with salary ranges based on external market data for the job’s level. Internal organization and peer data at Penn are also considered.

Equal Opportunity Statement

The University of Pennsylvania is an equal opportunity employer. Candidates are considered for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion, creed, national origin (including shared ancestry or ethnic characteristics), citizenship status, age, disability, veteran status or any class protected under applicable federal, state or local law.

Special Requirements

Background checks may be required after a conditional job offer is made. Consideration of the background check will be tailored to the requirements of the job.

University Benefits

Health, Life, and Flexible Spending Accounts: Penn offers comprehensive medical, prescription, behavioral health, dental, vision, and life insurance benefits to protect you and your family’s health and welfare. You can also use flexible spending accounts to pay for eligible health care and dependent care expenses with pre-tax dollars.
Tuition: Take advantage of Penn's exceptional tuition benefits. You, your spouse, and your dependent children can get tuition assistance here at Penn. Your dependent children are also eligible for tuition assistance at other institutions.
Retirement: Penn offers generous retirement plans to help you save for your future. Penn’s Basic, Matching, and Supplemental retirement plans allow you to save for retirement on a pre-tax or Roth basis. Choose from a wide variety of investment options through TIAA and Vanguard.
Time Away from Work: Penn provides you with a substantial amount of time away from work during the course of the year. This allows you to relax, take vacations, attend to personal affairs, recover from illness or injury, spend time with family—whatever your personal needs may be.
Long-Term Care Insurance: In partnership with Genworth Financial, Penn offers faculty and staff (and your eligible family members) long-term care insurance to help you cover some of the costs of long-term care services received at home, in the community or in a nursing facility. If you apply when you’re newly hired, you won’t have to provide proof of good health or be subject to underwriting requirements. Eligible family members must always provide proof of good health and are subject to underwriting.
Wellness and Work-life Resources: Penn is committed to supporting our faculty and staff as they balance the competing demands of work and personal life. That’s why we offer a wide variety of programs and resources to help you care for your health, your family, and your work-life balance.
Professional and Personal Development: Penn provides an array of resources to help you advance yourself personally and professionally.
University Resources: As a member of the Penn community, you have access to a wide range of University resources as well as cultural and recreational activities. Take advantage of the University’s libraries and athletic facilities, or visit our arboretum and art galleries. There’s always something going on at Penn, whether it’s a new exhibit at the Penn Museum, the latest music or theater presentation at the Annenberg Center, or the Penn Relays at Franklin Field to name just a few examples. As a member of the Penn community, you’re right in the middle of the excitement—and you and your family can enjoy many of these activities for free.
Discounts and Special Services: From arts and entertainment to transportation and mortgages, you'll find great deals for University faculty and staff. Not only do Penn arts and cultural centers and museums offer free and discounted admission and memberships to faculty and staff. You can also enjoy substantial savings on other goods and services such as new cars from Ford and General Motors, cellular phone service plans, movie tickets, and admission to theme parks.

jobs.title: Head of Communications
jobs.description:
About CloudWalk

We are not just another fintech unicorn.

We are engineers, designers, researchers, filmmakers, writers, and builders creating the financial infrastructure of the AI era.

Millions of people rely on our products every day. Behind them is an organization where AI isn't a feature—it is part of how we build, decide, communicate, and operate.

As our impact grows, so does the importance of telling our story with the same level of rigor, originality, and ambition that defines our products.

We're looking for a Head of Communications to build one of the most respected corporate communications organizations in technology.

Your Mission

Communications at CloudWalk is not a support function.

It is part of the product.

Your job is to help the world understand what we're building before everyone else does.

You will shape the company's narrative across media, founders, executives, product launches, research, AI, design, recruiting, investors, regulators, and culture.

You'll lead a multidisciplinary communications team while partnering closely with Design, Studios, Product, Engineering, Legal, People, Investor Relations, and Executive Leadership.

This role reports directly to the Chief Design Officer.

What You'll Do

Own CloudWalk's global communications strategy.
Define the long-term narrative that positions CloudWalk as one of the world's leading AI-native financial technology companies.
Lead external communications, PR, media relations, executive communications, thought leadership, corporate messaging, crisis communications, and internal communications.
Build compelling stories around products, technology, research, AI, infrastructure, entrepreneurship, and company milestones.
Partner with executives to develop speeches, interviews, keynote presentations, opinion pieces, and public appearances.
Lead communications for major launches, acquisitions, partnerships, fundraising, and strategic announcements.
Build trusted relationships with journalists, creators, analysts, investors, and industry leaders worldwide.
Drive proactive media strategy instead of reactive press management.
Develop measurement systems that connect communications efforts to business outcomes.
Build and mentor a high-performing communications organization with exceptionally high standards for writing, judgment, creativity, and execution.
Work closely with our internal creative and strategic teams to ensure every communication artifact reflects the quality of the products we build.
Use AI extensively to accelerate research, writing, planning, media intelligence, workflow automation, and organizational leverage.

What You Need to Succeed

Significant experience leading communications inside a technology company or agency supporting global technology brands.
Outstanding writing and editing skills.
Exceptional strategic judgment.
Experience advising C-level executives.
Strong understanding of global media dynamics.
Experience managing crises under pressure.
Ability to translate highly technical subjects into narratives that resonate with broad audiences.
Experience leading multidisciplinary teams.
Strong product intuition.
Comfortable working in ambiguity and creating structure where none exists.
High agency with a builder mindset.
Excellent English communication skills (written and spoken).

Nice to Have

Experience in fintech, AI, infrastructure, developer platforms, or deep technology.
Experience supporting major fundraising rounds, or public-company communications.
Strong relationships with international technology media.
Experience producing documentary-style storytelling, long-form editorial projects, or original research publications.
Experience working alongside design, creative, or film production teams.
Familiarity with AI-native workflows and modern communication tooling.

How We Work:

We believe communication should be as engineered as our products.

We value:

Intellectual honesty over spin.
Original thinking over trend-following.
Substance over noise.
Long-term reputation over short-term attention.
Craft over volume.
Ownership over process.

The Future We See

At CloudWalk, we believe every discipline will be transformed by AI.

Communications won't disappear, it will become dramatically more ambitious.

The best communicators won't simply write better press releases.

They will build narrative systems.

They will orchestrate humans and AI together.

They will discover stories before they happen.

They will help define how society understands entirely new technologies.

If that future excites you, we'd love to meet you.

Overview

Intuit — the global financial technology platform behind TurboTax, Credit Karma, QuickBooks, and Mailchimp — is seeking a Director Head of Global Public Affairs to lead and direct the company's global public affairs function. Based in Washington, DC and reporting to the Vice President of U.S. Federal Advocacy and Global Public Affairs, this executive owns Intuit's public affairs strategy at the global, federal, state, and local levels. The Director of Global Public Affairs is accountable for translating the Global Corporate Affairs and Public Policy (GCAPP) strategy into measurable business outcomes on behalf of Intuit's customers.

This is an executive leadership role. The Director defines the vision, strategy, and roadmap for the global public affairs function; leads a team of public affairs professionals; and exercises broad discretion over how Intuit tells the story of its customers to policymakers. The role leads the team responsible for paid media, strategic alliances, grassroots advocacy, third-party influencer outreach, and Intuit's political action committee (PAC) and policy association engagement — the campaign infrastructure that creates the conditions for Intuit's policy priorities to win.

This position serves as part of the GCAPP team and works directly with colleagues across Legal, Compliance, and Policy (LCPO), Intuit Brand and Marketing, Corporate Communications, Global Business Solutions Group (GBSG), Consumer Group (CG), and Corporate Responsibility teams.

This is a hybrid role with on-site expectations of 3 days per week in our Washington, DC office. We prioritize being together to promote connection and belonging, creativity and innovation, as well as speed, agility, and productivity to accelerate getting work done.

Responsibilities

Lead and build a high-performance team of six direct reports, and multiple external agencies, with a mandate to strengthen Intuit's brand and reputation among policymakers.
Develop and execute proactive, integrated public affairs communication strategies and content that articulate and support Intuit's legislative, regulatory, and public policy objectives, ensuring alignment with business priorities and reputation goals.
Oversee Intuit's political action committee (PAC) and policy association engagement, ensuring rigorous compliance, a clear political giving strategy, and alignment with the company's advocacy priorities.
Direct Intuit's grassroots and grasstops advocacy capability, mobilizing customers, employees, and allied voices in support of the company's policy objectives.
Build close, durable relationships with senior leaders across the LCPO organization and the broader business (including Intuit Brand Marketing and Corporate Communications), aligning Intuit's global public affairs objectives with concrete business outcomes and ensuring strategy moves in lockstep with business and reputational priorities.
Translate complex policy topics into accessible, persuasive narratives for policymakers, advocacy organizations, community groups, trade associations, think tanks, and media.
Identify opportunities, venues, and creative communications tactics to meet Intuit's objectives.
Strengthen message discipline, ensuring alignment across Public Affairs, Government Affairs, Legal, and functional partners.
Proactively identify and remove friction across and beyond Legal, Compliance, and Policy Organization (LCPO) to increase the velocity at which Intuit delivers for its global stakeholders.

Qualifications

Candidates must have a minimum of 15+ combined years of experience on political campaigns, in government work, or in public affairs and/or public relations with a major corporation, an agency, and/or trade association.
Experience working on political campaigns or in capitals — in the US or internationally — is preferred.
Proven track record of converting public affairs initiatives into concrete business results — measurable shifts in policymaker perception, coalition and grassroots scale, and campaign wins that created the conditions for legislative or regulatory outcomes.
Experience managing external agencies and significant campaign budgets, with accountability for results.
Familiarity with PAC operations and the compliance environment governing corporate political activity, or demonstrated ability to lead a regulated political program with the highest standards of integrity.
Strong writer, with the ability to distill key messages and present them in a compelling and visually interesting way. Proficiency with design, digital content production, and digital ad buying preferred.

Strong critical thinking and analytical skills, effectively analyzing and assessing opportunities and threats, prioritizing focus, and interpreting developments.
Capacity and drive to understand fully the business and operational elements of Intuit, including parsing what is mission critical from the trivial.
Ability to connect policy outcomes to business value by tying policymaker engagement and outcomes to the company's growth priorities.
Experience operating across multiple geographies and policy contexts.
Executive acumen, with experience advising and preparing senior executives for high-stakes policy engagements. Reputation for having the highest ethical standards and integrity.
Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree (JD, MBA, or master's in a relevant field) strongly preferred.
Willingness and ability to travel internationally as business needs require.

Footer

This position may be eligible for a cash bonus, equity rewards and benefits, in accordance with our applicable plans and programs (see more about our compensation and benefits at Intuit®: Careers | Benefits). jobs.title: Sr. Communications Manager
jobs.description:
Our Mission

As humans, there are few things more exciting than meeting someone new. At Tinder, we’re inspired by the challenge of keeping the magic of human connection alive. With tens of millions of users, hundreds of millions of downloads, 2+ billion swipes per day, 20+ million matches per day, and a presence in 190+ countries, our reach is expansive—and rapidly growing.

We work together to solve complex problems. Behind the simplicity of every match, we think deeply about human relationships, behavioral science, network economics, AI and ML, online and real-world safety, cultural nuances, loneliness, love, sex, and more.

Our Values

Take the Lead: We don't ghost our work or each other. Just as users don't leave their matches hanging, we don't let each other down.
Move Fast: We have a bias for action and urgency. Something that could be done tomorrow would be better if done today.
Better Together: We keep connection at the heart of dating and at the heart of how we work. Just as our users are better when they connect with others, so are we when we collaborate.
Real Talk: We say the hard thing the human way. Just as we ask our users to behave with kindness and candor in our community, we expect Team Tinder to do the same.
Safety First: We act with integrity, transparency, and consistency so people feel safe—whether they're swiping, matching, or working alongside us.
Spark Fun: We have fun to unlock creativity, fuel innovation, and help us build better experiences for daters.

Tinder is the most downloaded dating app in the world, and this is one of the most consequential product years in the company's history. Between IRL Events, Group Hangouts, a new visual identity, and a wave of features built to make dating feel more human, we're not just shipping updates, we're changing how people think about what Tinder is. This role exists to make sure the world notices.

There's never been a more exciting time to work at Tinder. We're doing something meaningful, helping people find their people, and this role sits right at the center of that story: translating product innovation into narratives that break through, backed by real data, told with real craft.

This is an opportunity to shape how Tinder shows up at the intersection of product and culture. You'll partner with Product, Product Marketing, Analytics, and Brand from the earliest stages of feature planning, not as someone who announces decisions already made, but as a communications partner in the room helping shape what the story is. ou'll also own the data side of the story yourself: spotting the angle inside a behavioral trend, getting it approved, and turning it into a pitch you take to press directly.

This role reports to the Head of Global Communications and operates from our New York office in a hybrid environment requiring in-office partnership 3x a week.

Where You’ll Work

This is a hybrid role and requires in-office collaboration three times per week. NYC or LA (preference for NY)

In This Role, You Will

Build and lead communications strategy for major feature launches, partnering with Product, Product Marketing, and Brand from early planning through launch day
Translate product improvements into stories consumers actually care about, why a feature makes dating better, not just what it does
Turn complex product areas into simple, credible narratives with clear proof points Spot creative, non-obvious angles in Tinder's product and behavioral data and turning them into pitchable stories that break through a crowded feed
Request and scope data pulls with Analytics, and shepherd every data-backed claim through approval (methodology, sample size, sign-off) before it reaches a reporter or agency
Packaging approved data and narrative for our PR agency partners to execute in-market pitch outreach
Bring comms' perspective into cross-functional launch planning early enough to help shape the story, flagging early when a narrative needs more definition or a claim isn't ready
Personally draft pitches and maintain your own press relationships

You'll Need

5+ years in communications, ideally spanning both product and consumer storytelling in consumer tech
A track record of hands-on management of feature launches with cross-functional teams, from strategy through placement
Sharp instincts for finding the signal in a roadmap or dataset before anyone else spots it
A real read on how the media landscape is shifting, and genuine curiosity about newer formats like podcasts and social-first reporters, not just the traditional trade and consumer press
Live media relationships. When a reporter emails, you're the one who picks up the phone
Comfort being in the room early with Product, Product Marketing, and Brand, not just receiving a brief after the fact
Enough data fluency to look at a pile of behavioral numbers or performance metrics and find the one angle that's a compelling story

Nice To Have

An agency background, and the hunger to grow inside a company that moves quickly
Experience navigating claims approval processes at a consumer tech company (working with Analytics or Legal to defend a stat before it goes external)
The range to work a product-feature story one week and a bigger brand or cultural story the next

As a Full-time Employee, You’ll Enjoy

Flexible Vacation, 10 Sick Days
Time off to volunteer and charitable donations matched up to $15,000 annually
Comprehensive health, vision, and dental coverage
100% 401(k) employer match up to 10%, Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP)
100% paid parental leave (including for non-birthing parents) and family forming benefits
Investment in your development: mentorship through our MentorMatch program, access to 6,000+ online courses through Udemy, and an annual $3,000 stipend for your professional development
Investment in your wellness: access to mental health support via Modern Health, paid concierge medical membership, pet insurance, fitness membership subsidy, and commuter subsidy
Free subscription to Tinder Gold

Commitment to Inclusion

At Tinder, we don’t just accept difference, we celebrate it. We strive to build a workplace that reflects the rich diversity of our members around the world, and we value unique perspectives and backgrounds. Even if you don’t meet all the listed qualifications, we invite you to apply and show us how your skills could transfer. Tinder is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace where we welcome people of all sexes, gender identities, races, ethnicities, disabilities, and other lived experiences. Learn more here: https://www.lifeattinder.com/dei

If you require reasonable accommodation to complete a job application, pre-employment testing, or a job interview or to otherwise participate in the hiring process, please speak to your Talent Acquisition Partner directly.

jobs.description:
Back to jobs

Communications Director

Los Angeles, CA

Who We Are

Atoms is building the machines that power the next era of progress.

Over the last decade, software has transformed the digital world. But the physical world, where food is made, minerals are mined, goods are moved, and industries are run, remains far less intelligent, far less efficient, and far more constrained. We’re changing that.

Atoms builds Physical AI— real-world robots for the industries that move civilization forward, starting with food, mining, and transport. Our systems are designed to understand, predict, and control the real world with precision, turning complex physical operations into something more reliable, more scalable, and more productive.

This work requires more than robotics. It requires deep integration across hardware, software, AI, operations, manufacturing, and real estate. We don’t just build machines in a lab. We deploy them into real environments, operate them, learn from them, and improve them until they work at scale.

We are roboticists, engineers, operators, and builders. We believe the next great technology companies will not only transform information, but the physical systems that shape everyday life.

If you want to work on hard problems with real-world impact, join us.

About The Role

We're looking for a senior communications leader to own the portfolio-wide comms layer across Atoms' Food, Mining, and Transport businesses, and to build the calendar and relationships that bring a coherent public narrative to a company operating in four very different industries at once (food, mining, transport, robotics).

The mandate is broad: set the strategy for how Atoms shows up across trade press, business press, and new media; build and run the network of vertical-embedded agencies and operators that makes that coverage happen; and make the calls on sequencing and tier as the company moves out of a long stretch of near-total media stealth. You will operate as a direct advisor to Atoms leadership on when and how each vertical's moments become public.

The right person has built a comms function from zero at a high-growth, product-and-regulator-adjacent company, reported directly to leadership, and turned a multi-faceted business into one coherent public narrative.

What You'll Do

Own the company-wide moment calendar, sequencing partnership announcements, fundraises, key hires, and first-site or product launches so they compound into a coherent story rather than compete with each other for attention.
Build and run the vertical media network, recruiting and managing boutique agencies and individual operators embedded in each industry's press ecosystem, in place of a single centralized firm covering all four.
Lead new-media strategy for Atoms leadership, identifying and securing placements with the top-tier and niche podcasts/shows/events most relevant to each vertical's audience.
Set channel and tier strategy, operating the existing architecture — newsroom as system of record, blog/Perspectives for thesis-level narrative, company LinkedIn for amplification.
Drive customer-forward storytelling, shifting the default from Atoms talking about its customers to structuring press moments where customers speak directly about their own growth — surfacing CloudKitchens, Picnic, or other Atoms companies.
Advise leadership directly on the timing, framing, and risk of every major public moment across a business where the wrong call carries real regulatory and partnership consequences.
Internal Communications: Own how Atoms communicates with its own people across four distinct businesses— major news, partnerships, hires, and launches from inside the company first.
Develop a crisis management playbook before it's needed, mapping the realistic risk scenarios across each vertical and have a response strategy ready for each.

What We Are Looking For

10+ years in communications, including direct experience building a comms function from zero at a high-growth company in a regulated or partnership-dependent industry.
A track record of reporting directly into leadership as a strategic advisor, not just an executor of a plan set by someone else.
Range across the full spectrum of comms work — product launches, funding announcements, executive comms, crisis response, internal comms — rather than depth in a single lane.
Experience managing a portfolio of boutique agency relationships in parallel, in place of one centralized firm of record.
The judgment to hold several distinct narratives at once — food delivery, mining, robotics — without collapsing them into one generic voice.
Sound instincts for substance-forward, low-combativeness media strategy, with an understanding of the asymmetric downside of an adversarial press strategy for a business built on partnerships and regulatory relationships.
Existing relationships in one or more of: restaurant tech, industrial/mining press, robotics and deep tech, or business/finance trade media.
Experience building new-media placement strategy for founders or executives.

Why join us

At Atoms, you’ll work on one of the defining challenges of our time—bringing automation into the physical world to drive real, lasting impact. We exist to uncover valuable unknown truths and turn them into progress, which means constantly pushing beyond what’s known and building what doesn’t yet exist. The work is ambitious and often challenging, but it’s grounded in a shared sense of purpose and a team committed to seeing it through together. Our work only matters if it serves others, and we know that meaningful progress depends on the trust of the people we serve and the strength of our team—so we invest in both, creating an environment where you can do your best work and grow.

What Else You Need To Know

This role is based in our Los Angeles office. Atoms is a company driven by invention and continuous change - we are constantly reimagining our industries, building new products, and refining how we operate. We do our best work together. That’s why all of our office-based teams work onsite, five days a week.

The base salary range for this role is $160,000 - $200,000 per year.

Actual compensation will be determined on an individual basis and may vary depending on experience, skills, and qualifications.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package. You may also be eligible for equity awards and an annual performance-based bonus.

Benefits Summary (USA Full-Time Exempt Employees)

Medical, dental, and vision insurance (multiple plans, incl. HSA options).
Company-paid life and disability insurance (short- and long-term).
Voluntary insurance: accident, critical illness, hospital indemnity.

8 paid holidays per year
Paid sick time

Paid Parental Leave

Benefits Are Subject To Change At The Company's Discretion.

Atoms accepts applications on an ongoing basis.

Job Openings Communications Consultant

About The Job Communications Consultant

About Empro Business Group

Empro Business Group are a boutique consultancy group focused on providing consultancy, recruitment, and technology solutions to the built environment sector.

Purpose
of the role

As a Communications Consultant, you will be a part of a project team working closely with a client to deliver effective change. As a subject matter expert in your field, you'll provide consultancy on strategic communications and engagement of stakeholders through a change journey. You'll take a lead role in stakeholder management and developing and managing internal and external communications approaches and plans, including training and new ways of working.

You'll need to think creatively and innovatively to design and deliver impactful communications that align to the projects key messages and tailored to key stakeholder groups. You'll have a nack for engaging and building rapport with clients, along with the ability to work to tight deadlines and budgets.

Responsibilities

Your responsibilities will encompass a range of critical tasks, including conducting thorough stakeholder analyses and client due diligence assessments to gain a comprehensive understanding of our client's unique needs. You'll then be responsible for developing and meticulously managing our communication approach and detailed plan, ensuring it aligns seamlessly with our project plan and key activities. Leveraging your expertise, you'll optimize the use of relevant communication channels, best practices, and the latest technology to deliver impactful communications that leave a lasting impression and call for repeat business.

Your role will also involve developing positive working relationships with key stakeholder groups through regular site visits and engagement activities. jobs.description:
About OpenAI Foundation

AI is already changing how people work, learn, and access care. It has the potential to unlock extraordinary benefits—faster medical breakthroughs, accelerated scientific discovery, more personalized services in healthcare and education, new tools for creativity and invention, higher productivity and economic growth, improved public services like transportation systems, and so much more.

But building powerful systems to benefit humanity is only a part of the work of our mission. Advanced AI models will also present new challenges that are already surfacing, and we need to be prepared to identify these challenges and develop solutions to address them.

These are the two dimensions of what we’re building the Foundation to do. We aim to enable the use of AI to find solutions to humanity’s hardest problems, transform what people are capable of, and deliver real benefits in people’s lives—while working hard with partners to be ready for new challenges, and to help make society resilient, as AI advances.

This work is just beginning. Over the next year, as we quickly ramp up, the Foundation expects to invest at least $1 billion across life sciences and curing diseases, jobs and economic impact, AI resilience, and community programs. This includes early investments toward our previously announced $25 billion commitment to curing diseases and AI resilience.

About The Role

The OpenAI Foundation believes that highly effective communication with the public is incredibly central to achieving the Foundation’s mission of ensuring artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. The Head of Communications will be a key leader at the Foundation, taking responsibility for the organization’s communications strategy and reputation.

What you'll do

Lead all internal and external communications, including media relations, thought leadership, executive visibility, crisis/issues management, and leadership and employee communications.
Help determine the long-term strategy and direction of the organization. Craft and communicate a vision.
Partner with senior leaders on strategic external positioning to increase their impact as organization advocates. Mentor other executives and spokespeople as they become more active in the public sphere.
Develop crisis management plans and procedures, and establish an infrastructure to take action as required rapidly. Develop thoughtful, strategic, and meaningful responses to time-sensitive press inquiries as they arise.
Act as the organization’s primary media liaison and organization spokesperson for significant initiatives. Represent the organization at media and corporate events.

Qualifications

Must be highly effective at developing and executing communications strategies for explaining the benefits of artificial general intelligence to the average member of the public.
Fifteen or more years of experience developing and executing successful communications strategies for industry-leading organizations. Experience in a fast-growing technology company is preferred.
Deep understanding of the media industry landscape and proven hands-on media relations experience with top-tier national media. A strong network of established contacts, combined with demonstrated skill and comfort in proactively building new relationships with top-tier media outlets worldwide.
Clear command of leading-edge communications, measurement, and analytics tools. Firm grasp of social media and the broader digital media landscape.
Proven experience operating on a global level with an international perspective and sensitivity to cultural nuances.
